transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Hi. I'm here because when I start eating, especially at night, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating anymore. It's just gotten to the point where it's really starting to scare me.

After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Also, during the episodes do you feel like the amount you eat is much larger than what most people would eat in a similar time?

Yes, it’s definitely way more than normal—I’ll easily go through two fast-food meals, a family-size bag of chips, and half a box of cereal in about an hour. Afterwards, I get so terrified of gaining weight that I force myself to throw up in the dorm bathroom or take laxatives, which happens a couple of times every week.
How long has this pattern of binge eating followed by vomiting or laxative use been happening, and does it occur at least once a week?

This whole cycle has been going on for about seven months, basically since my first semester at community college started. It definitely happens more than once a week—usually at least a couple of nights every week, especially since midterms last fall.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself? Are you very afraid of gaining weight even when others say your weight seems normal?

My whole self-worth is completely tied to my weight, and when I look in the mirror and see my stomach sticking out, I feel disgusted and like a total failure. Even when people tell me I look normal, I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight. I get so scared of seeing the scale go up the next morning that it completely consumes me.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent objectively large binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by recurrent compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting and laxative misuse) occurring at least weekly for about 7 months. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body weight/shape, with intense fear of weight gain. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.
